result.title: ViCARD: Visual Credit Assignment with Reward-Gated Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning
result.summary: Visual reasoning requires models to identify relevant visual evidence and use it to derive correct answers. Outcomebased reinforcement learning (RL) faces two key challenges in this regime: it yields no learning signal when perceptual errors cause all sampled responses to fail, and it broadcasts a uniform advantage across every token within a response. Conversely, while visual self-distillation offers dense guidance from evidence-centered image crops, student learning from token distributions alone often fails to elicit correct final answers. Motivated by an audit of training rollouts that exposes these complementary failure modes, we introduce ViCARD (Visual Credit Assignment with RewardGated Distillation), which integrates per-token visual supervision with verified correctness rewards. For each rollout group, we leverage a teacher with its input image cropped to the relevant visual area, and use this to provide per-token supervision to the student while also valuing correctness. If all sampled rollouts fail, ViCARD samples an additional crop-teacher answer and activates on-policy distillation only if that answer is correct. Together, these mechanisms provide fine-grained visual credit within informative reward groups and a learning signal for otherwise uninformative all-fail groups. Extensive comparisons across model scales demonstrate that ViCARD improves fine-grained visual reasoning performance over RL and distillation baselines, while retaining broad visual reasoning capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 ViCARD，将基于证据裁剪图像的教师逐 token 视觉监督与可验证正确性奖励结合，并在采样全失败时以裁剪教师的正确答案为门控条件启用 on-policy 蒸馏，用于多模态推理训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 逐 token 视觉信用分配与「答案是否真正使用视觉证据」的贡献分配问题直接相关，全失败组的奖励门控蒸馏也触及稀疏监督下的证据筛选；但监督落在输出分布而非 latent 推理状态，与 LVR 状态生成的联系待核查。
